_comment: Gap-harness synthetic breadth question set (#1125 §7). SME-authored ground truth: expected_facts are verbatim from the corpus _Verified: ...  citations so the grounded judge (§4) is anchored to module source of truth, never its own priors. Tags: 'exact-code' feeds the hybrid-lexical flip-threshold (§8); 'gated' exercises permission gating (#4); 'known-gap' has an expected_doc_id that is intentionally NOT in the corpus, to demonstrate corpus-gap discovery + the phase-5 round-trip. Keep expected_facts source-verified; do not add facts not backed by module source.

questions.query: what is the exact format of a VIN and which characters are not allowed
expected_facts: A VIN is exactly 17 characters matching ^[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}$: uppercase letters and digits with I, O, Q excluded.
The VIN system of record is pos-vehicle-inventory; it is stored raw (vin) and normalized (vin_normalized, globally unique).

questions.query: can a SKU be changed after a product is created and is there a required format
expected_facts: In pos-catalog the SKU is a client-supplied string, unique, required at create, and immutable thereafter.
There is no system-enforced length or regex pattern and no auto-generation for SKU; example values like SKU-12345 are illustrative only.

questions.query: which service owns purchase order numbers and what do they look like
expected_facts: Purchase orders are owned by pos-inventory (not pos-order).
A PO number is an 8-character, zero-padded, uppercase base-36 code from a Postgres sequence (e.g. 0000000A); there is no PO-/year prefix.

questions.query: what does an invoice number look like and what permission is needed to read an invoice
expected_facts: An invoice number is INV-<epochMillis>-<first 8 chars of the invoice UUID>, assigned once at draft creation.
Reading an invoice is gated by invoice:manage; there is no invoice:read permission.

questions.query: what is the format of a workorder number and how does it relate to the estimate number
expected_facts: A workorder number is WO-YYYY-NNNN with the sequence starting at 1000 (e.g. WO-2026-1001).
On promotion from an estimate it reuses the estimate's number with the prefix swapped (EST-YYYY-NNNN to WO-YYYY-NNNN) when free; estimate numbers are EST-YYYY-NNNN, unique per location.

questions.query: what is the format of a GL chart-of-accounts code
expected_facts: A GL / chart-of-accounts code (pos-accounting) matches ^\d{4}(-\d{3})?$: four digits, optionally a dash plus three digits (e.g. 1000, 4000-100).
The customer account number (pos-customer) is the party customerNumber, not a GL code.

questions.query: how do I look up the status of an order
expected_facts: Sales-order statuses (pos-order SalesOrderStatus) include DRAFT, QUOTED, COMPLETED, VOIDED, CANCEL_REQUESTED, and CANCELLED; read access is gated by order:order:view.

Purchase orders are NOT in pos-order — they are owned by pos-inventory (inventory:purchase_order:{create,view,approve,receive}) with PurchaseOrderStatus DRAFT, APPROVED, PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, FULLY_RECEIVED, CLOSED, CANCELLED.

questions.query: how are pricing rules and price books structured
expected_facts: Price precedence is a fixed sequential pipeline (PriceQuoteServiceImpl.calculatePrice): BASE_PRICE (MSRP, required) then LOCATION_OVERRIDE (absolute replacement) then CUSTOMER_TIER_DISCOUNT (multiplicative), with final rounding HALF_EVEN at scale 2.

effectiveFrom is inclusive and effectiveTo exclusive (NULL = open-ended/active); within one rule type the most-recently-effective active record wins. Read-level pricing permissions are pricing:price_book:view and pricing:rule:view.

how do I read the NLTI audit trail for a request
what is the policy for processing a customer return and issuing a refund on a paid invoice
expected_facts: Returns are line-by-line against one COMPLETED sales order, per-line capped at the un-refunded remainder; creation parks in PENDING_APPROVAL when the total refund exceeds the approval threshold (default $250.00), otherwise RETURN_REQUESTED.

Refund methods are ORIGINAL_TENDER, STORE_CREDIT, and ON_ACCOUNT_CREDIT; ORIGINAL_TENDER reverses the original settled tender and a failure parks the return at REFUND_FAILED before any stock movement.
